races.title: State House, District 80
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Sam Watford
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 80 (Davidson County area). Underground utility contractor by trade. Served in the House 2015–2019 and again since 2021. Earlier served three terms as a Davidson County Commissioner and sat on the county Planning and Zoning Board.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Watford was born or raised, or when he came to North Carolina. The dates of his county commissioner service were not given. We found no statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, school choice or teacher pay, or policing. His 2014 campaign site said he would monitor residential, commercial and industrial growth and described himself as pro-business, but that is too general to match to a specific position. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2024 or 2026. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

cands.name: JacQuez Johnson
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 80 in 2026. He advanced from a canceled primary and lost the general election to incumbent Sam Watford (R). The sources available give no information on his occupation or offices held.

endorsements.text: Listed as endorsed by the voter guide group "Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy" (Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he came to North Carolina. We could not find his occupation, work history or any office he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign platform, interviews or public statements on data centers, development, taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing. We found no news coverage of him and no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond one voter guide group.
